memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the country. 'For otherwise,'
they said, 'we will all die!' So the people took their dough before the yeast
was added, and carried it on their shoulders in kneading troughs wrapped in
clothing." - Ex 12:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Egyptians who had once refused to let Israel go now cannot get them out fast
enough. God had said Pharaoh would "drive you out completely" (Ex 11:1), and
here it is, exactly so.

And there is a small, homely detail: the people carried their dough on their
shoulders, wrapped in clothing, because there was no time for it to rise.

I love that picture. It is not grand. It is a family scooping up a bowl of half
made bread and hurrying out the door. God's great acts of deliverance arrive in
the middle of ordinary domestic life. There were babies to carry, animals to
gather, neighbours to call. Redemption happened in the middle of the household.

Notice also that they were ready. They had eaten with their sandals on, exactly
as instructed. When the moment came at last, they were not scrambling to prepare
because they had already obeyed.

Obedience beforehand is what makes readiness possible afterwards. The families
who took the instructions seriously that afternoon were the families who could
move at midnight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What preparation is God asking of you now, before you can see why?
2. Do you look for God mainly in the dramatic, or also in the ordinary?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to obey today in the small things, so that I am ready when You
move. Thank You that You work in the middle of ordinary life. Amen.
